title: Single-use confirmation links (only the checksum is stored)
interface:
namespace Drupal\hwdesk\Service; final class HandoverTokens (declare(strict_types=1)).
Rewrite. The previous version signed the link with the site key, so the link could always be recomputed from the database row. The link is now a random secret and the database keeps only its checksum: a leaked database row cannot be turned back into a working link, and a used link stops working.
Constructor: __construct(\Drupal\Core\Entity\EntityTypeManagerInterface $entityTypeManager, \Drupal\Component\Datetime\TimeInterface $time). Registered in hwdesk.services.yml as 'hwdesk.handover_tokens' with arguments ['@entity_type.manager', '@datetime.time'] (already written; do not touch).
The handover entity type id is 'hwdesk_handover' (class \Drupal\hwdesk\Entity\Handover). Fields you need: 'token_hash' (string, max_length 64), 'user' (entity reference to the employee), 'expires' (timestamp), plus getStatus(): \Drupal\hwdesk\HandoverStatus and getExpires(): int.
Public methods -- keep these exact signatures, HandoverService::confirmUrl() calls issue() with three arguments:
- issue(int $handoverId, int $uid, int $expires): string -- make a fresh link. Take 32 bytes from random_bytes() and encode them base64url WITHOUT padding: rtrim(strtr(base64_encode($raw), '+/', '-_'), '=') gives exactly 43 characters of [A-Za-z0-9_-]. Load handover $handoverId from storage, set its 'token_hash' to hash('sha256', $token) (64 lowercase hex characters), save the handover, return the token (never the checksum). Calling it again replaces the stored checksum, so the previously issued link stops working. The $uid and $expires arguments are legacy and MUST be ignored -- the employee and the expiry are read from the stored handover, never from the caller. A handover id that does not exist -> \InvalidArgumentException whose message names the id and contains neither the token nor the checksum.
- verify(string $token): ?array -- return ['handover' => int, 'uid' => int, 'expires' => int] taken from the stored handover, or NULL. Return NULL whenever: the string does not match /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}$/D; no handover has token_hash = hash('sha256', $token); the handover's status is not \Drupal\hwdesk\HandoverStatus::Pending; or its expires is smaller than $this->time->getRequestTime(). 'uid' is (int) the id of the handover's user, 'expires' is (int) its expires field. Check the shape with the regular expression BEFORE hashing, so junk never reaches the database.
- consume(string $token): void -- the link is single use. Find the handover the way verify() does but without the status and expiry conditions, clear its 'token_hash' (NULL or '') and save it. An unknown, malformed or empty token is ignored in silence: this runs while a page is being answered, so it must never throw.
Look the handover up with an entity query on the 'token_hash' field: $this->entityTypeManager->getStorage('hwdesk_handover')->getQuery()->accessCheck(FALSE)->condition('token_hash', $hash)->range(0, 1)->execute(). accessCheck(FALSE) is deliberate -- the visitor who clicks the link in the e-mail is not logged in. Never load every handover and filter in PHP.
No logger, no \Drupal:: static calls, no echo or print, no var_dump: the token must not reach a log, an exception text or the screen. Nothing else in the class is public.

Clock (new): the only clock in this class is the injected $this->time->getRequestTime(). Never call time(), date(), new \DateTime(), \Drupal::time() or any other wall clock, not even for logging or for a comparison you think is harmless. The acceptance test measures expiry against that very same injected clock; a class that reads the wall clock instead answers differently depending on how long the process has already been running, which is how a link that expired a second ago can still look valid.

uses.Handover entity: web/modules/hwdesk/src/Entity/Handover.php: the fields and getters named above

database: The handover entity storage through the injected EntityTypeManagerInterface (sqlite under the hood); no direct SQL.
forbidden: Keeping the old HMAC design or the PrivateKey service: a link that can be recomputed from the database is exactly what this rewrite removes.
Putting the token or its checksum into an exception message, a log entry or any other field of the handover.
Writing hwdesk.services.yml, the entity class or the test.
